ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, January 20, 1962, as extensively amended), Articles 288-316; The Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, September 27, 2001, as amended) and its Enforcement Decree; the Financial Services Commission's Supervisory Guidance on Customer Due Diligence and Beneficial Ownership Identification; and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 5559, as amended) for UBO piercing and the filing of foreign investment reports.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Registrar of Companies / Companies Registry in the ultimate beneficial owner's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize in the issuer's country; then, if the issuer is an Apostille Convention member, obtain a Hague Apostille and submit directly to Korean authorities without consular legalization. If the issuer is a non-member, obtain legalization by the Republic of Korea's embassy or consulate in that country; the consular path is exclusive and must never be chained to an apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Government corporate registry / tax office in the legal entity's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize in the issuer's country; Apostille member states use the Hague Apostille while non-member states require Korean consular legalization. The two authentication paths are parallel and mutually exclusive and no sequential combination is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of each corporate shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certify by corporate secretary, notarize locally, and then apply either the Hague Apostille (member state) or Korean consular legalization (non-member state). Submit the authenticated original to Korean counsel; a copy must accompany the Certificate of Good Standing.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent registry or notarial office where the existing legal entity is registered
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain a certified copy or notarized extract; Apostille member states proceed under Hague Apostille; non-member states proceed through Korean consular legalization only. Never append consular legalization to an apostilled document or vice versa.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship or correspondent bank of the UBO/legal entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Letter must be notarized and signed by an authorized bank officer; for Apostille member states attach a Hague Apostille, while for non-member states the bank executes Korean consular legalization. Submit within 90 days of issuance; the same authentication-path rule applies entirely and no hybrid route is permitted.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All prospective directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners shall be screened against (i) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (iii) Korea's Financial Action Task Force (FATF) public statements; (iv) the domestic sanctions list administered by the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs; (v) Interpol Red Notices; and (vi) dedicated PEP databases maintained by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU). Screening must be re-run in real time and before each transaction or account opening; any adverse hit must be escalated to the Compliance Officer, and enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs, family members, close associates, and beneficial owners from high-risk jurisdictions. Evidence of each screening result must be retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IrosGo) of the Republic of Korea
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered trade name of a Chusik Hoesa must be written in Hangul in the commercial register. Any foreign-language brand or business name must be converted into a Hangul phonetic transliteration, and the legal-form suffix must read Chusik Hoesa. The standard four-tier structure is: (1) distinctive trade-name element; (2) business-scope descriptor; (3) brand, trademark or geographic modifier; and (4) mandatory corporate-form suffix. The Hangul registered version controls over all English or romanized versions and must satisfy the Registry's criteria for distinctiveness and non-confusion.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must first obtain a written rejection notice stating the legal basis. Within 14 days, it may file an administrative appeal with the head of the registry and the Minister of Justice under the Administrative Appeals Act; alternatively, a direct lawsuit may be filed in the Administrative Court within 90 days under the Administrative Litigation Act. The appeal must submit a corrected proposed name, evidence of prior use or trademark registration, and a comparison of all same or confusingly similar names in the same jurisdiction. If the registry does not issue a decision within 30 days, the applicant may treat the application as rejected and pursue judicial review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Commercial mailbox/virtual office is not per se prohibited at company registration stage for low-risk ISIC 4791 subscription-box commerce; however, the National Tax Service accepts a business place for VAT purposes only when there is a physical office and supporting documents (lease contract, utility bills, business inventory, personnel or operational records). Major banks likewise require an in-person visit and physical place of business before opening a corporate account. A pure virtual office will likely result in denial of business registration and refusal of a corporate bank account; therefore a serviced office or shared workspace with individual office number, lease in the company's name and mail-handling service is strongly recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (a) registered address is on the lease and utility bill; (b) personnel are present during normal business hours; (c) inventory/fulfillment space is identifiable; (d) tax invoices and bank statements are stored on-site; (e) the business does not use a residential apartment without conversion. Quantified risk: for a low-risk subscription box business, the probability of unannounced municipal or tax inspection within 24 months is approximately 15%; if three or more checklist items are absent, the probability rises to 40% or higher, and the National Tax Service or district tax office may request documentary proof within 30 days.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company trade name search and clearance application at the Internet Registration Office
Notarization of Articles of Association for Chusik Hoesa
Pre-incorporation corporate and AML/CFT KYC due diligence by Korean counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market-rate fixed fee; hourly benchmark USD 350-500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO identification and ownership structure matrix, including piercing of shell layers and confirmation of ownership threshold
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for UBO diagrams and source-of-funds analysis

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization handling, translation, and international courier for authenticated bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent Hague Apostille authority or Republic of Korea embassy/consulate plus courier service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government fee schedule plus actual out-of-pocket courier cost

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registry filing fee and certificate issuance after successful name clearance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Court fee schedule plus registration tax (0.4% of capital) and education surcharge

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000 of 1962, as consolidated through Act No. 20336 of 2024), particularly Articles 289 (articles of incorporation), 295 (deposit of subscription payments), 317 (application for incorporation registration), 383 (board of directors), 489 (statutory auditor), and the Commercial Registration Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registry Office of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the company, operating through the Supreme Court-regulated Commercial Registration System (IROS). For Seoul, the competent office is the Seoul Central District Court Registry Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Stock Corporation (Commercial Registry Form), together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, subscription statements, minutes of the organizational meeting, and written acceptances of statutory officers.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in share capital applies to a Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act. However, the full amount paid for issued shares must be deposited with a Korean bank before incorporation registration, and the bank must issue a balance certificate naming the corporation; such deposit must remain blocked until registration is completed. The fee estimate above assumes a nominal issued capital of KRW 100,000,000, yielding approximately USD 385 in consolidated registry tax, education surtax, and court stamp duty. No separate escrow-account rule is imposed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the first meeting of the Board of Directors of the corporation, duly convened at the registered office with a quorum, is hereby recorded as follows; and all action items below are adopted as binding corporate resolutions. 1. RECORDING OF INCORPORATION AND ISSUANCE OF SHARES. The Board acknowledges receipt of the certified incorporation registration of the Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea at the District Court Registry Office. The total number of issued ordinary shares, each with the par value stated in the Articles of Incorporation, is confirmed. The Board ratifies the subscription list, confirms full receipt of statutory contributions, and directs the Representative Director to issue share certificates in accordance with Commercial Act Articles 355 through 365. 2. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. The Board adopts [Registered Office Address], South Korea, as the corporation's sole registered legal address for service of process and governmental notices. The Representative Director is directed to maintain the corporate seal and registration extract at this address and to file any relocation amendment with the competent registry office within the statutory period. 3. BANKING AND TREASURY AUTHORIZATION. The Board authorizes the opening of one or more corporate bank accounts with licensed Korean financial institutions, including domestic won and/or U.S. dollar settlement accounts to support Stripe Billing and Authorize.Net pay-ins. The Representative Director, jointly with one additional director designated by the Chief Executive Officer, is authorized to sign account mandates, wire instructions, payment service agreements, and treasury instruments. This authorization remains in force until revoked by a subsequent board resolution. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The Board appoints [Name] as Representative Director, [Name] as Director and Chief Executive Officer, and, if required by the Commercial Act or the Articles of Incorporation, [Name] as Statutory Auditor. The officers accept office as evidenced by their written acceptances included in the registration dossier. The Board delegates day-to-day management, e-commerce compliance, and subscription-box fulfillment operation to the Chief Executive Officer, subject to supervision by the Board. 5. GENERAL IMPLEMENTATION. The Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer are jointly authorized to execute and submit the incorporation registration, tax business registration, e-commerce mail-order seller notification, environmental and civil defense license applications, and all ancillary notices; to pay official fees; and to retain legal counsel. These resolutions are effective immediately and continue until modified by a proper board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation Name Clearance and Court E-Filing Account Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Attached Internet Registration of Corporations (IROS) Portal, www.iros.go.kr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Check the IROS corporate name database before drafting the Articles. Because the commercial registry will reject an application if the name is identical or confusingly similar to an existing company in the same registry, the filing attorney should obtain a printout of the name search. When the name is cleared, register the client's digital certificate for the court e-filing system and assign the application to the registry with jurisdiction over the proposed registered office. This step is preliminary but materially reduces the risk of a correction order and avoids re-notarization.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name in Korean and English
Representative director's passport or alien registration card
GPKI digital certificate for court e-filing
Proposed registered office address and land register extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is unavailable because of an identical or confusingly similar existing registration, select an alternative name and resubmit the search; no statutory appeal is available for a name-search rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public certified in the Republic of Korea and registered with the Korea Notary Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in the Korean language containing the corporate name, corporate purpose, address of the registered office, total authorized shares, calculation of issued shares, par value, call methods, board composition, and auditor provisions as required by Commercial Act Article 289. All incorporators must execute the Articles before a notary public, who must verify identity, confirm that the incorporation procedures are lawful, and issue a notarial certificate. The notarized Articles are the decisive document for the registry examination and cannot be amended after filing except by special shareholder resolution.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Initial written resolution on incorporation terms
Proof of identity or legal-entity certificate of each incorporator
Power of attorney for foreign incorporators and legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary public requires amendments, correct the draft and re-execute before the same or another notary; a notarized document may not be altered without re-execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription and Blocked Bank Deposit of Share Payments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed bank or postal depository in the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoters must subscribe for at least one share each and cause the full amount of the shares issued as payment in cash to be deposited in a bank account in the corporation's name. The bank must issue a balance certificate confirming the deposit and holding it at the disposal of the corporation until registration is completed. Any in-kind contribution must be transferred to the provisional officers before registration and evaluated by an examiner unless exempted by the court. The board shall verify the deposit certificate before filing the registration application.
required_dossiers: Subscription list with subscriber names, addresses, and number of shares
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank balance or deposit certificate issued in the name of the corporation
Minutes of the statutory organization meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deposit certificate is challenged for insufficient particulars, obtain a corrected certificate from the bank; if subscriptions are undersubscribed, close the deposit, revise the subscription list, and deposit the corrected amount.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry Office of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office, accessible through the IROS commercial registration system or in person
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for registration of incorporation with the competent District Court Registry using the official commercial registry forms. The application must state the corporate name, registered office, paid-in capital, issued shares, directors, statutory auditor, and representative director. Attach the notarized Articles, subscription statements, bank deposit certificate, minutes of the statutory organization meeting, written acceptance of office from each director and auditor, and a power of attorney if filed by legal counsel. The registration officer conducts a legality review and may issue a correction order. On completion, the registry issues a certified corporate registration extract and corporate seal certificate.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation of a stock corporation
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Stock subscription report and bank deposit certificate
Minutes of the incorporators' and first board meetings
List of directors and statutory auditor with written acceptances
Power of attorney to the local filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order (bojung myeongryung), comply within the court's stated period by filing the missing or corrected documents; if registration is refused, rectify and re-file or file an immediate appeal under the Non-Contentious Cases Litigation Procedure Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Business, E-Commerce, and Physical Facility Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (Hometax), competent local government for e-commerce notification, local fire safety authority, and Ministry of Employment and Labor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 21 calendar days from incorporation registration, file the corporate business registration with the National Tax Service through Hometax and obtain a business registration certificate. For subscription-box commerce, submit the mail-order seller notification to the competent local government under the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce and Mail-Order Transactions, stating the categories of subscription merchandise and consumer dispute resolution contact. If warehousing and packaging operations are established, apply for a building use and occupancy certificate, submit a workplace establishment report to the Ministry of Employment and Labor, and complete civil defense fire safety inspections or approvals before any physical handling. If products are imported, coordinate with licensed customs brokers separately.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of corporate registration extract
Certificate of corporate seal
Lease or ownership evidence for warehouse and office
Corporate business registration certificate
Mail-order seller notification form
Warehouse floor plan and fire safety design documents
Occupational safety and health workplace establishment report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the local government queries the mail-order seller notification, correct the prohibited-goods declaration or consumer dispute resolution mechanism and resubmit; if a fire safety inspection fails, remedy the identified violation and apply for reinspection before commencing physical operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; primary electronic portal: Home Tax Service (HTS) at https://www.hometax.go.kr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Chusik Hoesa incorporated in Korea, the company obtains its statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT Business Registration Number through the standard Korean business registration process. After court registration at the local Commercial Registration Office, the statutory representative files a business registration application with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the principal place of business; registration is submitted in person or electronically through the Home Tax Service. The district tax office issues the Business Registration Certificate containing the ten-digit Korean TIN, which simultaneously serves as the VAT registration number. A foreign non-resident entity without a Korean registered address that is nonetheless liable for Korean tax or VAT must appoint a tax agent with a domestic address and file the Korean non-resident business registration application with the NTS district tax office; the NTS then issues the same Business Registration Number where a permanent establishment or VAT collection obligation exists. Foreign electronic-commerce operators can use the simplified HTS foreign entity registration window to obtain a VAT registration number for services supplied to Korean customers when no domestic establishment is present.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a US-style check-the-box election or a separate pass-through election for a Chusik Hoesa. A Korean stock corporation is mandatorily treated as a separate corporate income taxpaying entity under the Corporate Income Tax Act. The Korean hybrid mismatch rules operate by compulsory statutory adjustment rather than taxpayer election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold applies to a Chusik Hoesa; VAT registration is mandatory from the commencement of business, regardless of turnover. A simplified VAT registration threshold of KRW 80 million annual gross revenue is limited to qualifying individual sole proprietors and is not available to an incorporated stock corporation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Tax invoices must be issued for all VAT taxable supplies. Electronic tax invoices must be transmitted to the NTS through the Home Tax Service certified electronic invoicing system or an NTS-certified API-connected ERP system. The NTS does not employ a pre-clearance fiscal stamp model, but taxpayers must transmit e-tax invoice data to the NTS by the end of the next business day after issuance to enable near-real-time cross-matching. The NTS also requires mandatory tax invoice key fields, digital signature or certification, and multiple issuances are monitored for abnormal invoice sequences under the integrated tax information system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Korean Chusik Hoesa may claim the 0% VAT rate for physical goods that are delivered to a foreign destination as genuine exports under the Value-Added Tax Act, including recurring subscription boxes dispatched by international courier or freight forwarder. The claim requires that the goods leave the Korean customs territory and that payment is made or settled in foreign currency by the overseas buyer. For bundled digital content, advertising services, or domestically consumed services accompanying the subscription box, an appropriate apportionment is required and the zero-rating applies only to the exported tangible goods component, not to local services or rights that are used in Korea.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic Export Declaration acceptance issued by Korea Customs Service through the UNIPASS customs clearance system
Commercial Invoice describing the subscription box contents, harmonized system codes, quantities, and export unit prices
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing shipment from Korea to the foreign destination
Subscriber order records and recurring billing schedule demonstrating the cross-border commercial transaction
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) / Foreign Currency Receipt Confirmation issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank
For postal or small-parcel exports, the postal export customs declaration or international shipment tracking documentation accepted by Korea Customs Service
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service may jointly audit export zero-rating claims. If the customs declaration, transport evidence, or foreign-exchange receipt evidence is missing, false, or inconsistent, the claimed 0% rate is clawed back and the full 10% VAT is assessed on the export supply, together with statutory interest and overdue additional tax. Falsifying export documentation or claiming zero-rating on goods not actually exported may subject the entity to further additional taxes, civil penalties for fraudulent tax invoices, and criminal referral under the Frame Act on National Taxes and the VAT Act. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day statutory period may also cause the sale to be recharacterized as a domestic supply and expose the company to exchange-control penalties under Korean foreign exchange regulations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK) in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won (KRW) is fully convertible for current account transactions, including trade-related payments, service fees, royalties, and ordinary business remittances, subject to documentary verification by designated foreign exchange banks. Capital account transactions are more tightly controlled. Foreign direct investment into a Chusik Hoesa requires reporting under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and the foreign exchange bank must verify the inward remittance against the investment report before issuing a capital verification certificate. Profit remittances such as dividends are permitted once corporate tax is settled and board shareholder resolutions are documented, but the remittance must carry proper purpose codes and be processed through a designated foreign exchange bank. There is no general surrender requirement forcing conversion of all export proceeds into KRW; exporters may maintain foreign currency accounts, but all receipts must be repatriated through the domestic banking system and reported. For a subscription box business, recurring inbound payment flows from overseas e-commerce gateways such as Stripe Billing and Authorize.Net create temporary suspense balances that must be reconciled and sequentially traced to the underlying sales invoices. The Bank of Korea maintains exchange rate stability through managed floating, and any capital outflow beyond prescribed thresholds requires a certificate of tax payment and remittance approval from the foreign exchange bank. Practical hurdles include strict anti-money-laundering (AML) profiling of foreign shareholders, physical presence expectations for signatories, and the need for clear source-of-funds dossiers for every capital injection.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act rules, export proceeds for goods or services generally must be collected within six months from the date of export, unless an extension is granted by the designated foreign exchange bank due to justified commercial reasons. There is no fixed mandatory conversion ratio into KRW; exporters are allowed to deposit foreign currency proceeds into a domestic foreign currency account, but the receipt must be reported and settled through a bank authorized to handle foreign exchange transactions. Failure to repatriate within the statutory timeline triggers regulatory inquiry and possible administrative penalties, so a subscription box operator must reconcile gateway settlement batches and convert/repatriate proceeds in compliance with the six-month rule.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational KRW/USD Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Currency Account with multi-currency sweeps
Foreign Investment Capital Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Foreign Exchange Settlement Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a primary treasury rail. Domestic Korean financial regulators do not license foreign digital EMI platforms to hold KRW deposits or provide local clearing account IBANs. Offshore digital banks and EMI issuers cannot substitute for a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Payment gateways such as Stripe Billing and Authorize.Net can be used only for the collection of card payments from end customers, and the settlement proceeds must be routed into a Korean licensed bank account. Using an unlicensed fintech EMI for treasury operations would create licensing, AML, and foreign exchange reporting violations. A supervised partnership with a domestic Tier-1 bank is mandatory for capital verification, export receipt processing, and outbound supplier payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean banks generally require the authorized signatory and ultimate beneficial owner to appear physically in-branch for the initial KYC interview when the entity is a newly formed Chusik Hoesa with non-resident shareholders. Remote consular proxy opening is not a standard approval path and is rarely accepted for new foreign-invested companies. Some banks may accept a notarized and apostilled power of attorney only after the initial face-to-face interview has been completed and the bank’s compliance committee has pre-cleared the ownership structure. For this Stage 4 blueprint, the treasury officer must plan a physical visit to Seoul for at least one representative director, and must bring corporate documents authenticated by Korean notary and apostille, board resolutions, passport copies of all beneficial owners, and a detailed source-of-funds disclosure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders and beneficial owners with opaque corporate chains causing failure to identify the natural person controlling the Chusik Hoesa.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a complete corporate ownership and control chart up to the individual natural persons, certified copies of registry extracts, apostilled certificates of incorporation, notarized passports of all shareholders with 25% or greater ownership, bank references for each material shareholder, and written declarations of source of initial capital, including three months of bank statements showing the funding trail for each subscription account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious recurring monthly revenue pattern from overseas payment gateways labeled as subscription box sales, with potential exposure to third-party payment aggregation and layered settlement structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver signed payment processing agreements with Stripe Billing and Authorize.Net, gateway settlement statements for at least six months, merchant site identification, PCI DSS attestation of compliance, customer order logs, shipping manifests, logistics carrier contracts, and a reconciliation framework proving that each inbound settlement batch matches identifiable subscription orders and does not represent pass-through third-party funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High cross-border transaction velocity with payments originating from multiple jurisdictions including jurisdictions perceived as higher risk for e-commerce AML screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a sanctions screening policy, IP-based geoblocking configuration, automated AML transaction monitoring system description, customer risk scoring methodology, and a list of blacklisted shipping countries. Provide evidence of end-customer verification, including email, phone, and address verification, plus the company’s policy for rejecting transactions from sanctioned jurisdictions and for performing enhanced due diligence on any high-risk shipping address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large lump-sum foreign direct investment inflows into an escrow account followed immediately by rapid outbound payments for inventory and logistics, creating a layering-like flow.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the Foreign Investment Report filed with the Ministry of Economy and Finance, the designated foreign exchange bank’s capital verification certificate, board resolutions authorizing the capital injection, commercial contracts with suppliers and logistics providers, proforma invoices, purchase orders, customs declaration forms, and cash flow forecasts aligning the injection with operating expenditures and preventing co-mingling of personal and corporate funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be executed as SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from the overseas parent or investor to the Chusik Hoesa’s designated foreign exchange bank account. Each transfer must reference the Foreign Investment Report filed with the Ministry of Economy and Finance and use the appropriate purpose code for equity investment. The receiving bank will verify the beneficial owner, reconcile the remittance message to the share subscription resolution, issue a capital verification certificate, and report the transaction through Korea’s Foreign Exchange Information System. After capital verification, the funds are transferred from the temporary escrow account into the operating KRW account. For refinancing or interim working capital, additional remittances require amended foreign investment reporting and source-of-funds disclosure.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements should be processed through SWIFT MT103 for supplier payments, royalties, and subscription content licensing fees. Purchase of physical goods for subscription boxes should use Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) issued by the Korean bank for major inbound inventory shipments, while smaller recurring logistics payments can be handled by SWIFT MT103 with supporting invoices and customs declarations. Documentary Collections are acceptable for low- to medium-risk suppliers with established trade relationships. Every outbound remittance must be tagged with the correct export/service settlement purpose code and supported by a sales invoice, transport document, tax invoice, and intra-group agreement where relevant.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Export/import-linked forward foreign exchange contracts with a Korean bank, limited to the amount and tenor of actual subscription box trade receivables and payables
Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts against KRW only when the corporate has a verified real trade exposure, marked-to-market and subject to bank approval
Cross-currency interest rate swaps and FX swaps for matched commercial payment flows, not for speculative positions
FX options with physical delivery, permitted when fully covered by documentary evidence of export proceeds or import payment obligations, and disapproved for naked speculative positioning

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (including separately prepared financial statements, tax adjustments, and the audit report if applicable) submitted through the HomeTax e-filing portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a company with a 31 December year-end, the base deadline is 31 March of the following year, with an automatic one-month extension to 30 April available when an external audit is required or when an extension is granted by the NTS under the Framework Act on National Taxes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing/under-reporting penalty of 20% of the unreported tax amount; late-payment surcharge of 0.03% per day on the unpaid tax; for deliberate evasion, criminal fines up to KRW 100 million (approx. USD 77,000) and imprisonment up to 5 years. Prolonged failure may lead the NTS to seize corporate assets and the court to issue a judicial dissolution and administrative strike-off order under the Commercial Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surtax return (municipal surtax on the national corporate tax) submitted to the competent local government tax office via WeTax.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Government (Si/Gun/Gu tax office where the registered head office is located)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, on or before 30 April of the following year (or the corresponding extended deadline if the national corporate tax deadline is extended).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A penalty equal to 20% of the unpaid local surtax; additional daily interest of 0.025% of the unpaid tax; consecutive failures may result in attachment of corporate bank accounts and, after repeated non-payment, a court order for involuntary dissolution of the Chusik Hoesa.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Shareholders (AGM) - convening and holding the meeting, adoption of financial statements, appointment/re-appointment of directors and external auditors, and completion of any required registrations in the Commercial Registry for newly appointed directors/auditors.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry (District Court) for registration of director changes; AGM minutes retained at the registered office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held within 3 months of the fiscal year-end (by 31 March for a 31 December year-end); any change in directors/auditors must be registered with the Commercial Registry within 2 weeks of the general meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to hold the AGM by the deadline are subject to an administrative fine under Article 635 of the Korean Commercial Act of up to KRW 5,000,000 (approx. USD 3,800); failure to register a director change within 14 days attracts a non-compliance fine of up to KRW 5,000,000 per incident; habitual default may cause the court to strike off the company after judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-annual Value-Added Tax (VAT) returns - one for the first half (January-June) and one for the second half (July-December), filed with invoices and purchase statements.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half return filed 1-25 July; second half return filed 1-25 January of the following year (small e-filers may straddle the deadline as prescribed by the NTS).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 20% of any under-reported or unreported VAT; daily delay charge of 0.03% of the unpaid VAT; repeated failure can lead to seizure of business property, revocation of the business registration, and, with continued non-operation, administrative strike-off from the commercial register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report (independent certified public accountant's report on the financial statements) prepared under the External Audit Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) and, as appropriate, the Financial Supervisory Service; a copy is also filed with the NTS together with the corporate tax return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The auditor must complete and submit the report to the company no later than 6 weeks before the AGM (mid-February for a calendar-year company holding its AGM by 31 March); the company must file the report with the FSC within the period prescribed by the External Audit Act (normally within 2 weeks after the AGM).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If a company subject to audit fails to appoint an auditor, an administrative fine of up to KRW 20 million (approx. USD 15,400) may be imposed; directors may be fined up to KRW 5 million (approx. USD 3,800). The FSC may order a re-audit and impose sanctions on the auditor; persistent failure to maintain the audit is viewed as gross negligence and may support an administrative dissolution order.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (statutory marginal rate for taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion; progressive brackets: 10% up to KRW 200 million, 20% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 22% from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: General incentives include the Research & Development (R&D) tax credit (up to 50% of qualifying R&D expenditures for SMEs), investment tax credits under the Tax Incentives Limitation Act, and special economic zone or foreign investment zone benefits. No patent box regime applies to subscription box commerce; however, standard business expense deductibility and reduced tax rates for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) may lower the effective rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Tax Return (법인세과세표준 및 세액계산서) filed via the Home Tax Service (HTS) e-filing system (www.etax.go.kr); the electronic form is designated as the final annual corporate tax return on the HTS portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal year basis); semi-annual prepayment filings are required by the end of the second month following the first half of the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The final corporate tax return must be filed within 3 months from the close of the fiscal year (e.g., for a 31 December year-end, the deadline is 31 March of the following year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total sales and ordinary business income, including subscription receipts, shipping fees, and ancillary merchandise revenue, recognized on an accrual basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where revenue includes cross-border sales to related non-resident distributors or intercompany services, ensure arm's-length pricing under the International Tax Adjustment Act; exclude intercompany dividends or capital gains that are separately reported on Box 4.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of book income (net profit per financial statements) to taxable income by adding non-deductible expenses and subtracting exempt or temporary difference items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-resident shareholders (e.g., excessive interest, royalties) that exceed arm's-length amounts are non-deductible for tax purposes and may trigger remittance withholding obligations; properly disclose and substantiate the business reason for each cross-border payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 (Applicable Tax Rate and Calculated Tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of progressive statutory tax rates to the computed taxable income bracket, yielding the base corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If foreign tax credits are claimed, compute the credit limit proportionally against Korean corporate income tax; do not offset any withholding tax deducted on behalf of non-resident payees against this entity's own tax liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for qualifying asset investment credits, R&D credits, foreign tax credits, and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credit is only available for income taxes paid to foreign jurisdictions on income also subject to Korean tax; documentation, including a Tax Residency Certificate and detailed foreign tax return, must be retained for at least 5 years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting of foreign income taxes that will be claimed as credits (or deductions) against Korean corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a subsidiary of a foreign parent, any taxes withheld on downstream dividends from Korea are not this entity's taxes and must be reported separately by the non-resident shareholder; this box only covers foreign taxes on the Korean entity's own foreign-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amounts already paid as semi-annual prepayments and any tax withheld at source by customers or domestic payers on local income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that all withholding taxes withheld on behalf of non-resident employees or shareholders are properly reported and remitted on separate WHT returns; these amounts cannot be credited against this entity's corporate tax prepayments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file by the statutory deadline triggers an additional tax penalty equal to 20% of the unpaid tax if the return is filed more than one month late, or 10% if filed late before the tax is paid; in addition, a daily delinquency charge of 0.03% applies to the unpaid amount from the original due date until full settlement. Intentional fraud or evasion is prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act, with imprisonment of up to 2 years or a fine of up to twice the evaded tax, and the company and its de facto directors may be assessed civil surcharges up to 40% of the tax avoided.
